players.product: The Generate Platform (machine-learning generative biology; computational design integrated with large-scale biological experimentation) and AI-engineered protein therapeutics such as GB-0895

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 Phase 1 asthma results (ERS poster furnished on 8-K; study GB-0895-101, unblinded Parts A and B, data cutoff 26Jan2026): 80 participants with mild-to-moderate asthma in the single-ascending-dose part (10 mg to 1200 mg, 3:1 vs placebo) and 16 in the multiple-ascending-dose part (300 mg or 600 mg Q12W x 2). GB-0895 was well tolerated with no treatment-related SAEs: any TEAE 66 (95.7%) on GB-0895 vs 26 (96.3%) on placebo, any serious TEAE 1 (1.4%) vs 2 (7.4%), injection-site reactions 10 (14.5%) vs 4 (14.8%), all ISRs Grade 1; the 3 SAEs (1 GB-0895, 2 placebo) were all Grade 3 and none related to GB-0895. PK was sustained and dose-proportional with a half-life of about 98 days at 300 mg, with no evidence of target-mediated drug disposition or of anti-drug antibodies affecting half-life. The poster concludes that 300 mg achieves maximal suppression of the PD biomarkers BEC, FeNO, IL-5 and IL-13 for at least 6 months, that doses above 300 mg show no meaningful improvement, and that a single subcutaneous 300 mg injection exhibits broad anti-inflammatory activity for at least 6 months, supporting a dosing regimen of one subcutaneous injection every 6 months. Generate designed GB-0895 with ~20-fold higher affinity for TSLP than tezepelumab and YTE Fc modifications for extended half-life (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: half-life ~98 days at 300 mg; any TEAE 95.7% vs 96.3% placebo; serious TEAE 1.4% vs 7.4%; 300 mg maximal PD suppression for at least 6 months; ~20-fold higher TSLP affinity than tezepelumab

quarterly_data.signal: GB-0895 COPD results (ERS poster; Phase 1 study GB-0895-101 Part C, blinded data, data cutoff 27Jul2026): 40 adults with COPD and blood eosinophils of at least 200 cells/uL received a single dose of 300 mg (n=15) or 600 mg (n=15) or placebo (n=10); 39 remain on study and all completed at least 10 months of follow-up. GB-0895 was well tolerated with no treatment-related SAEs: in blinded results with GB-0895 and placebo pooled, any TEAE 29 (72.5%), any serious TEAE 5 (12.5%) with 6 SAEs in 5 participants, none above Grade 3 and none related to GB-0895 / placebo, ISRs 3 (7.5%), all Grade 1. PK was comparable between asthma and COPD. Reductions from baseline in BEC, FeNO, IL-5 and IL-13 were seen as early as Month 1 and sustained for at least 6 months, and 300 mg gave PD biomarker suppression comparable to 600 mg. One participant was excluded from the PD data as a baseline outlier; Generate says analyses including this participant do not alter the conclusions and that the complete data were provided to regulatory authorities.
quarterly_data.figure: N=40 (300 mg n=15, 600 mg n=15, placebo n=10); any TEAE 72.5% and serious TEAE 12.5% (blinded, GB-0895 and placebo pooled); no treatment-related SAEs; PD reductions sustained for at least 6 months

quarterly_data.signal: SOLAIRIA Phase 3 design (ERS poster): SOLAIRIA-1 (NCT07276724) and SOLAIRIA-2 (NCT07359846) are ongoing global, replicate, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled registrational studies of adjunctive GB-0895 in adults and adolescents (age 12 to 80) with severe uncontrolled asthma and at least 2 exacerbations in the prior 12 months, with no restriction on blood eosinophils (all-comers); N=786 subjects randomized 2:1 over 52 weeks of treatment, with an optional open-label extension. The primary endpoint is the annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) over 52 weeks; key secondary endpoints include AAER in patients with baseline eosinophils below 300 cells/uL, FEV1, AQLQ(S)12+, ACQ-6, time to first exacerbation and symptom scores. The poster states the Phase 1 study showed reductions in BEC, FeNO, IL-5 and IL-13 for at least 6 months with magnitude comparable to tezepelumab monthly doses (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: N=786 randomized 2:1; primary endpoint AAER over 52 weeks
